title: Phased Handoff Arbitrator with rollback credit pool and health-bucketed cohorts
author: Sofia Ramos
description:
Motivation: As customers run increasingly complex multi-cohort rollouts and frequent experiments, we see two recurring problems: (1) noisy transient regressions trigger cascade rollbacks that waste capacity and delay experiments, and (2) aggressive automated rollback policies can exhaust safety margins for dependent services. This PR introduces a Phased Handoff Arbitrator: a small runtime component that mediates handovers between model versions using health-bucketed cohorts and a configurable rollback credit pool.

What this implements: the arbitrator adds two cooperating mechanisms. First, cohorts are assigned to health buckets (green/yellow/red) based on a short-window composite health score (latency p95, error rate, model-quality regression signal). The bucket system lets the orchestrator apply graded handoffs: green cohorts get fast commits, yellow cohorts receive slower phase gates with extra sampling and telemetry, red cohorts go into shadow-only until healed. Second, rollback credit pool is a tenant-scoped budget that limits the number/rate of automatic rollbacks within a time window; credits are consumed on each rollback and regenerate over time. When credits are low, the arbitrator prefers graded mitigation (traffic hold, session-drain) and escalates to on-call only after a higher threshold.

Key changes: single continuous change set across orchestrator, scheduler, and the control-plane policy engine with associated tests and docs. High-level:
- new service: orchestrator/handshake/arbitrator.go (PhasedHandoffArbitrator implementation, policy evaluation, credit pool ledger)
- policy: policy/arb_policy.yaml (default thresholds, credit regen rate, bucket mapping)
- runtime hooks: scheduler/handoff_adapter.go (cohort annotation, holdpoint creation, graceful drain API)
- telemetry: observability/metrics_arbitrator.prom (bucketed counters, credit pool gauge, per-tenant counters)
- console: ui/rollouts/handovers.md (user guide for configuring credit pools and health buckets)
- tests: integration/arb_integration_test.go, unit tests for credit ledger and bucket scoring

Backward compatibility & migration: default configuration keeps the previous behavior for tenants without policies (arbitrator is opt-in via a tenant flag). For tenants that enable it, we migrate current ongoing rollouts into the arbitrator's phased flow on next deploy; a short windowed replay runs existing active sessions to rebuild cohort affinity metadata. Admins can set credit_pool.capacity=0 to disable automated rollback gating (rollbacks still possible via manual /oncall).

Operational considerations: the credit pool model is intentionally conservative. We tuned defaults based on simulations (see linked Linear ticket) to avoid blocking legitimate emergency rollbacks. The arbitrator emits metrics for: credit_consumed, credit_remaining, cohort_bucket_transition, handoff_duration_ms, and suppressed_rollback_events. Grafana dashboards and alert rules were added in observability/alerts/arbitrator.rules.yaml.

Security & privacy: credit pool ledger stores only aggregated counts by tenant and 1h sliding windows. No inference inputs are recorded. Access control respects existing RBAC; only rollout_admin and infra_sre roles can set global policy overrides.

Testing summary: local unit tests cover scoring boundaries and credit regeneration; integration tests simulate 3-tier cohort mixes with synthetic latency/error injection. CI pipeline ran with a short-canary smoke test in staging against a 50k request replay and validated safety gates prevented noisy rollbacks while preserving prompt-regression detection.

Performance: The arbitrator runs in-memory and uses lock-free counters for the credit pool; benchmarks in perf/arb_bench.go show median additional latency for a handoff decision is <0.6ms at 10k qps, and memory overhead is ~2MB per arbitrator shard.

Rollout plan: staged rollout to Canary clusters (10% of tenants) for 72h, then to Beta (40%) for 7 days, then full release. During Canary and Beta we keep credit_pool.capacity at conservative defaults (2 credits per hour).

Notes on rationale: the credit-pool idea came from incident post-mortem SUP-1298 where repeated automatic rollbacks created flapping and blocked subsequent safe experiments. The bucketed cohorts help reduce blast radius while keeping experiments moving.

Files changed (high-level):
- orchestrator/handshake/arbitrator.go (new)
- orchestrator/handshake/arb_types.go (new)
- policy/arb_policy.yaml (new default)
- scheduler/handoff_adapter.go (mod)
- scheduler/handoff_adapter_test.go (new tests)
- observability/metrics_arbitrator.prom (new metrics)
- observability/alerts/arbitrator.rules.yaml (new alerts)
- ui/rollouts/handovers.md (new doc)
- integration/arb_integration_test.go (new)
- perf/arb_bench.go (new)
- Makefile (mod: add bench target)

Merge outcome: squash-merged into main after approvals. CI initially reported a flaky test (scheduler/handoff_adapter_test.go) which was fixed in a follow-up commit included in this PR. All checks green after the fix.

Why this PR is different from previous rollout work: Instead of only throttling traffic or using single-step canaries, this introduces an explicit budgeted safety mechanism (rollback credits) combined with graded cohort semantics. That combination is intended to reduce oscillations while preserving fast recovery when necessary.

Related work and follow-ups: follow-up tasks created: ENG-5057 (dashboard refinements), ENG-5099 (expose credit pool via Console UI controls), ENG-5106 (HA coordination for arbitrator shards).

If reviewers want a demo: I can run a short recorded 10-minute replay showing how credits are consumed and how yellow-bucket cohorts get phased through extra sampling.

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Can we make the credit regen configurable per-tenant? Some enterprise tenants will want stricter limits.
Author (Sofia): Yes — added tenant-level override in policy/arb_policy.yaml and documented in the UI guide.

Priya Desai: We should ensure arbitrator decisions are traceable in request traces for debugging.
Author: Added a trace tag (arb.handoff.bucket) and score fields to the tracing span in the scheduler adapter.

Liam O'Connor: Concern about shard coordination during network partitions.
Author: Added light HA notes in the follow-ups (ENG-5106) and conservative defaults that avoid cross-shard coordination for credits (credits are per-tenant-per-shard for now).
release_notes: Introduce Phased Handoff Arbitrator with health-bucketed cohorts and rollback credit pool. Opt-in for tenants. Adds metrics and dashboards. See ui/rollouts/handovers.md for configuration and migration notes.
notes_for_oncall: If a tenant reports blocked rollouts, check arbitrator.credit_remaining and arbitrator.suppressed_rollback_events. Use the admin override to temporarily increase credit_pool.capacity or manually trigger rollback as needed.
